label: History
value: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls Harbor in the summer.
unit: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls Harbor in the summer to recuperate at Lorna Vane's home following a bout of typhoid fever and to visit the ancestral homestead built by his grandfather, John Tremayne. Upon meeting Captain Saul, Adrian was introduced to the captain's written logbook and agreed to collaborate on adapting his life story into a novel. During the summer, he spent his mornings writing at the lighthouse and his afternoons exploring the coast with Lorna, Nell, and Hugh Carrow. In the process, he fell deeply in love with Lorna Vane, though he kept his feelings secret out of respect for her situation regarding her husband, Rufus. Before departing Seven Gulls in the autumn to return to Toronto, he confessed his heartbreak to Nell. He later successfully published the novel based on Captain Saul's life, which achieved widespread critical and commercial success.

value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lived in Brierley

Throughout Nell's childhood and school years, Mrs. Agatha offered advice, attended community events like the Sunday-school picnic, and participated in political trips to Port Marlow. Upon learning that Obed and Thirza Abernethy intended to adopt an orphan boy, she immediately visited Grey Shutters to investigate and express her misgivings. When Obed instead brought home Nell Harcourt, Mrs. Agatha criticized the decision and later visited to inspect the child, only to be met with a passionate outburst from Nell after bluntly calling her plain and red-haired. Though initially offended, she forgave Nell completely when the girl offered a dramatic, humbling apology at her home, and she eventually grew quite fond of her. Throughout Nell's childhood and school years, Mrs. Agatha offered advice, attended community events like the Sunday-school picnic, and participated in political trips to Port Marlow. After the passing of her quiet husband, Thomas Sowerby, she faced financial hardship due to farm mortgages, leading her to move into Grey Shutters with Thirza Abernethy, where she set up her own quarters in the former spare room.

label: History
value: Ambrose Kerr is a Liberal.
unit: During an election fifteen years prior, Ambrose Kerr, a passionate Liberal, publicly swore not to shave his beard or trim his hair until his party achieved a political victory [v04:c09:p0018]. He kept this vow faithfully, growing an extraordinarily long beard and hair that made him a well-known local oddity [v04:c09:p0013, v04:c09:p0023]. During a stormy November evening, he met Nell Harcourt on the road after agreeing to a political deal with Tobias Corcoran, though he later assured Nell he would vote according to his principles [v04:c09:p0061, v04:c09:p0071]. When the Liberals finally won a landslide election, Ambrose immediately went to the local barber in the middle of the night to be shaved and groomed [v04:c09:p0035]. Shortly afterward, he renewed his long-standing courtship of Miss Winifred Tolley, and the two agreed to marry [v04:c09:p0025, v04:c09:p0028].

He kept this vow faithfully, growing an extraordinarily long beard and hair that made him a well-known local oddity [v04:c09:p0013, v04:c09:p0023]. During a stormy November evening, he met Nell Harcourt on the road after agreeing to a political deal with Tobias Corcoran, though he later assured Nell he would vote according to his principles [v04:c09:p0061, v04:c09:p0071]. When the Liberals finally won a landslide election, Ambrose immediately went to the local barber in the middle of the night to be shaved and groomed [v04:c09:p0035]. Shortly afterward, he renewed his long-standing courtship of Miss Winifred Tolley, and the two agreed to marry [v04:c09:p0025, v04:c09:p0028].

label: History
value: Anthony Tulk attended the local school
unit: Anthony Tulk attended the local school in Brierley. After Nell Harcourt began teaching, he showed continuous disdain and disrespect toward her due to his belief that female teachers were useless. He regularly tested her patience, glaring at her with insolence and mocking her behind her back. One day, after placing a live mouse inside Nell's desk to startle her, he openly admitted his responsibility with an impudent laugh. Pushed past her limit, Nell lost her temper and whipped him with a hardwood pointer. Although Nell felt deep shame and regret for losing her self-control, the punishment earned Anthony's respect. The next morning, Anthony greeted her politely, offered to carry her books, and admitted to his peers that she was capable of delivering a beating 'as good as a man's.' From that point on, he stopped giving her trouble, worked hard in class, and developed a genuine fondness and respect for her.

One day, after placing a live mouse inside Nell's desk to startle her, he openly admitted his responsibility with an impudent laugh. Pushed past her limit, Nell lost her temper and whipped him with a hardwood pointer. Although Nell felt deep shame and regret for losing her self-control, the punishment earned Anthony's respect. The next morning, Anthony greeted her politely, offered to carry her books, and admitted to his peers that she was capable of delivering a beating 'as good as a man's.' From that point on, he stopped giving her trouble, worked hard in class, and developed a genuine fondness and respect for her.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house
unit: Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house when her daughter married and departed for missionary work. Mabel Colby proposed that she come to Portmaris to keep house at Tabby's Place for Mabel, Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay during their final years at Wexcombe College. She agreed and moved to Portmaris, bringing along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph. During her time at Tabby's Place, she provided a warm, comfortable, and indulgent home for the students. After the girls graduated from college, she chose to remain in the house for the summer to care for the cats rather than visit relatives, before eventually traveling to India to visit her daughter's mission field.

label: History
value: Barney drove Nell Harcourt to the Sunday-school picnic
unit: Barney initially drove Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke to the Sunday-school picnic using the sorrel mare. Later, he drove a double-seated buggy carrying his sister Odette, Nell, and Isolde to the concert at the Debating Club hall. He also drove Nell, Isolde, and Odette to a concert and supper at the Pale Sands Hotel, though he fled to the team out of dread of attending the social supper. When his father bestowed the upper farm on him, he sought a wife. Too shy to ask Nell Harcourt directly, he persuaded his sister Odette to propose to her on his behalf. Upon Nell's rejection of the proposal, he promptly married Nettie Scobie, and their marriage was published ("appeared out") in church shortly thereafter.

He also drove Nell, Isolde, and Odette to a concert and supper at the Pale Sands Hotel, though he fled to the team out of dread of attending the social supper. When his father bestowed the upper farm on him, he sought a wife. Too shy to ask Nell Harcourt directly, he persuaded his sister Odette to propose to her on his behalf. Upon Nell's rejection of the proposal, he promptly married Nettie Scobie, and their marriage was published ("appeared out") in church shortly thereafter.

label: History
value: Belinda began working as a maid for Miss Rosalind Penrose
unit: Belinda began working as a maid for Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage when she was thirteen years old. She readily accepted Miss Rosalind's quirk of calling her 'Belinda the Fourth' after her three older sisters who had previously held the post. She frequently helped Miss Rosalind with her romantic imaginings, such as blowing a tin horn and giggling to produce echoes in the forest for visitors like Nell and Isolde. When Stephen Stanhope returned to court Miss Rosalind, Belinda excitedly supported the romance. She helped prepare Echo Cottage for Miss Rosalind’s wedding, where she threw an old shoe that accidentally hit Mr. Wace. Following Miss Rosalind's marriage, Belinda planned to move to Boston with her and Mr. Stanhope.

label: History
value: Captain Saul spent fifty years roaming the globe as a sea captain.
unit: Captain Saul spent fifty years roaming the globe as a sea captain, surviving numerous shipwrecks, fires, and mutinies. Over fifty years prior to his death, he lost his young sweetheart, Margaret, to the sea during a sudden squall, a tragedy that led him to remain unmarried for the rest of his life while cherishing her memory. In his later years, he retired from the sea and became the lighthouse keeper at Seven Gulls Point. He maintained a close friendship with the young newlyweds Nell and Hugh Carrow, sharing his rich life stories and welcoming them into his circle of 'kindred spirits.' Later, he provided the material and inspiration for Adrian Treleaven to write his published biography. After thirty years of tending the Seven Gulls lighthouse, Captain Saul passed away peacefully in his sleep at the age of seventy-six, resting with his finished 'life-book' in his hands.

label: History
value: Cedric came to Brierley
unit: Cedric came to Brierley from the United States to reside with his grandmother on the shore road. He quickly bonded with the local schoolteacher, Nell Harcourt, recognizing her as a kindred spirit who understood his imaginative nature and grief over his mother's death. Later, he formed a warm friendship with Miss Rosalind Penrose of Echo Cottage. After his father returned from the States, Cedric continued to excel in school, write poetry, and participate in the local story club.

value: Flossie attends the Brierley school.

When Nell is punished by Mr. Pidgeon, Flossie grins at her humiliation. Later, when Nell returns to school, Flossie attempts to mock her, but her taunts are met with silent forgiveness. Flossie joins the Regent's entrance class, boasting that she attends school merely for an education as her father's wealth means she will not need to work. She competes in school recitations, though she expresses disdain for the events due to her lack of creative mind, and she becomes moody upon losing the role of Fairy Queen to Odette Pullen. After taking her entrance exams in Portmaris, she barely passes with a three-point margin. She subsequently attends Regent's Academy for a second year of study.

She competes in school recitations, though she expresses disdain for the events due to her lack of creative mind, and she becomes moody upon losing the role of Fairy Queen to Odette Pullen. After taking her entrance exams in Portmaris, she barely passes with a three-point margin. She subsequently attends Regent's Academy for a second year of study.

label: History
value: Hugh spends three childhood years in Alberta.
unit: Hugh grows up in Brierley, having spent three childhood years in Alberta with his father. Upon returning from a summer in New Brunswick, he re-enters Brierley school, where he becomes a fierce academic rival to Nell Harcourt after pulling her braid and getting her slate broken over his head. Though he apologizes, Nell holds a grudge against him, even when he defends her to the teacher or tries to offer gifts. Hugh attends Regent's Academy alongside Nell, entering the advanced classes and competing closely with her for top honors. He later serves as the president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society, advocating for local beautification projects. To pay for his medical degree at Wexcombe College, he works as a schoolteacher at Pale Sands. At Wexcombe, he excels academically, becomes Captain of the Freshman football team, wins the Cooper Prize, and earns High Honors in Classics. During his university years, he repeatedly attempts to declare his love to Nell, but she initially turns him down due to her own romantic illusions. After nearly dying of typhoid fever at Seven Gulls, Hugh recovers and resumes his medical career, taking over his great-uncle's practice in Glen St. Agnes. Following his recovery, he and Nell reconcile, acknowledge their mutual love, and become engaged. They marry in the Grey Shutters orchard and move into a small white house by the shore at Seven Gulls.

label: History
value: Isolde grows up at Pear Hill
unit: Isolde grows up at Pear Hill in Brierley. After returning from a visit to her aunt in Delford, she meets Nell Harcourt and the two instantly swear a solemn oath over an imaginary stream of running water to be bosom friends for life. They spend their days playing together at 'Larkrise' in the birch grove, naming local landmarks, and sharing books and stories. Isolde attends the Brierley school alongside Nell, excelling in subjects like geometry. After accidentally consuming Thirza's currant wine and becoming intoxicated, her strict mother temporarily forbids her from playing with Nell, leading to a dramatic farewell between the two girls before the misunderstanding is resolved. Later, during a sleepover at Pear Hill, Isolde and Nell accidentally jump onto the bed occupied by her visiting great-aunt Lavinia, though the incident ultimately ends in amusement and reconciliation.

label: History
value: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls.
unit: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls in a poor but loving family. Tragedy struck early when her younger brother Julian was killed in an accident, and two years later her beloved father committed suicide. Determined to make a life for herself and her frail mother, Lorna studied at Regent's Academy and became a successful teacher at the Glen school. However, when she was sixteen, Rufus Vane threatened her mother with foreclosure, coercing Lorna into marrying him. Shortly after, her mother died, and Rufus went to sea on the Four Sisters. When the ship failed to return, he was presumed dead, but Captain Saul later discovered him in Havana, suffering from complete amnesia caused by a head injury. Brought back to Seven Gulls, Lorna spent eleven years faithfully caring for him as an invalid child. After Nell Harcourt moved to Seven Gulls, the two formed a deep, life-changing friendship that brought Lorna back to life. Eventually, Dr. Hugh Carrow realized Rufus's condition could be cured through surgery. Lorna bravely agreed to the operation. The procedure succeeded in restoring his memory, revealing a startling truth: the man Lorna had been caring for was actually Rufus's cousin, Laurence Vane, and the real Rufus had died in Cuba years before.

However, when she was sixteen, Rufus Vane threatened her mother with foreclosure, coercing Lorna into marrying him. Shortly after, her mother died, and Rufus went to sea on the Four Sisters. When the ship failed to return, he was presumed dead, but Captain Saul later discovered him in Havana, suffering from complete amnesia caused by a head injury. Brought back to Seven Gulls, Lorna spent eleven years faithfully caring for him as an invalid child. After Nell Harcourt moved to Seven Gulls, the two formed a deep, life-changing friendship that brought Lorna back to life. Eventually, Dr. Hugh Carrow realized Rufus's condition could be cured through surgery. Lorna bravely agreed to the operation. The procedure succeeded in restoring his memory, revealing a startling truth: the man Lorna had been caring for was actually Rufus's cousin, Laurence Vane, and the real Rufus had died in Cuba years before.

label: History
value: Isolde lives at Pear Hill
unit: Isolde lives at Pear Hill in Brierley. After returning from a visit to her aunt in Delford, she meets Nell Harcourt and the two quickly swear a solemn vow of lifelong friendship over an imaginary stream. She and Nell share a playhouse called Larkrise and participate in numerous imaginative adventures. When her mother mistakenly believes Nell intentionally got Isolde intoxicated on homemade currant wine (which Nell had mistaken for raspberry cordial), Isolde is forbidden from playing with Nell, leading to a dramatic farewell. However, after Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup during a winter emergency, Mrs. Pembroke pardons Nell and allows the girls to resume their bosom friendship. Isolde later attends the local Brierley school alongside Nell, partakes in schoolhouse dramas, Sunday-school picnics, and community events, and ultimately becomes engaged to Gideon Duckett.

value: Mabel Colby attended Brierley school
unit: Mabel Colby attended Brierley school, where she befriended Nell Harcourt and offered to teach her a design for knit lace. She later attended Regent's Academy and pursued studies alongside Nell and Hugh Carrow, earning recognition as the beauty of the Second Year class. After completing studies at Regent's, she taught at an isolated rural school for several years, facing the typical trials of a country schoolteacher. Desiring to escape the monotony of country boarding and further her education, she applied to Wexcombe College for the Sophomore class. She proposed to Nell and Honora Hollis that they rent a house together in Portmaris to manage their own meals, bringing along her Aunt Euphemia as a housekeeper. The plan succeeded when they secured Tabby's Place, where Mabel took up residence alongside Nell, Honora, Cressida Lindsay, and Aunt Euphemia for their final years of university.

label: History
value: Nell was brought to St. Brendan's Island
unit: Brought to St. Brendan's Island by mistake instead of an orphan boy, Nell was taken in by the bashful siblings Obed and Thirza Abernethy at Grey Shutters. Though initially unwanted due to her gender, her bright spirit and vivid imagination quickly won over both siblings, as well as her lifelong bosom friend Isolde Pembroke and neighbor Agatha Sowerby. Attending Brierley school, Nell excelled academically while engaging in a fierce academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow, though she briefly boycotted school after breaking a slate over his head for calling her 'Carrots.' She formed a story club, organized the Brierley Village Improvement Society, and saved the life of little Posy Fay Pembroke during an attack of croup. Winning the prestigious Avery Scholarship at Regent's Academy, she chose to delay college to teach at Brierley school and support Thirza at Grey Shutters after Obed's sudden death. Later, Nell earned her B.A. with High Honors in English at Wexcombe College while living with friends at 'Tabby's Place.' Returning to Brierley to teach, she eventually reconciled her feelings for Hugh Carrow, agreeing to marry him. Following their wedding, they moved to a seaside cottage in Seven Gulls Harbor. Nell suffered the tragic loss of her firstborn daughter, Joyce, shortly after birth, but eventually found solace and joy in raising her second child, James Obed (Little Kit).

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy lived a quiet life
unit: Obed Abernethy lived a quiet life at Grey Shutters with his sister Thirza. Seeking farm assistance due to his advancing age and heart trouble, he and Thirza arranged to adopt a young boy from an orphanage in Nova Scotia. When Obed traveled to Alder River station, he discovered that a girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake instead. Unable to leave her behind, he brought her to Grey Shutters and quietly insisted on keeping her despite Thirza's initial objections. Obed quickly formed a deep bond with Nell, enjoying her chatter and often intervening when Thirza was strict. Over the years, he showed Nell great affection, buying her treats and secretly purchasing a stylish dress with puffed sleeves for her Christmas gift. Shortly before Nell was due to attend college, news arrived that the Abbey Bank, where Obed kept all his savings, had failed. The shock caused Obed to collapse and die instantly of a heart attack in his doorway, leaving his family to mourn a kind and gentle man.

When Obed traveled to Alder River station, he discovered that a girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake instead. Unable to leave her behind, he brought her to Grey Shutters and quietly insisted on keeping her despite Thirza's initial objections. Obed quickly formed a deep bond with Nell, enjoying her chatter and often intervening when Thirza was strict. Over the years, he showed Nell great affection, buying her treats and secretly purchasing a stylish dress with puffed sleeves for her Christmas gift. Shortly before Nell was due to attend college, news arrived that the Abbey Bank, where Obed kept all his savings, had failed. The shock caused Obed to collapse and die instantly of a heart attack in his doorway, leaving his family to mourn a kind and gentle man.

label: History
value: Odette Pullen grew up in Brierley.
unit: Odette Pullen grew up in Brierley and attended the local school. She was part of the older students' group preparing for Regent's Academy entrance examinations and was courted by the schoolmaster, Mr. Pidgeon. She was a member of the local youth circle, participating in Sunday-school events, picnics, and literary/story clubs. She passed her entrance exams alongside her peers and moved to Port Marlow to study at Regent's Academy. After completing her studies, she took a teaching position in Stonebridge. She later decided to move to western Canada to teach. While there, she met and married Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman with mining interests in Winnipeg. She returned home to Brierley briefly before her wedding, where she married Mr. Inglis in a grand ceremony before moving to a mansion in Winnipeg.

label: History
value: Opal grows up in Brierley.
unit: Opal grows up in Brierley and attends the local school alongside Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke. At school, she is known for her beauty and her habit of flirting with the boys, as well as her susceptibility to drama and tears. After finishing her early schooling, she attends Regent's Academy in Port Marlow to train as a teacher. Following a bout of congestion during the winter after her time at Regent's, her health begins to fail rapidly due to galloping consumption. Though she attempts to remain cheerful and insists she will return to teaching, she is forced to give up her school post at Pale Sands. In her final months, she admits her deep fear of death to Nell Harcourt and expresses her longing to live a normal life. She passes away quietly in her sleep during the late summer.

label: History
value: Pettifer purchased the Robert Bell farm in Brierley.
unit: Pettifer purchased the Robert Bell farm in Brierley and moved there from New Brunswick, quickly establishing a reputation as an eccentric bachelor who kept house alone. He engaged in a feud with Agatha Sowerby after making blunt remarks to her when she solicited donations for missions. Later, he became infuriated when Nell's Jersey cow repeatedly broke into his oatfield, confronting Nell directly. However, after Nell accidentally sold his cow to a buyer, he surprisingly accepted the mistake with humor and agreed to trade cows with her, leading to a warm friendship between them. Soon after, his estranged wife Emily returned to live with him, restoring tidiness to his household. Tragically, his pet parrot Nutmeg was killed by lightning during a severe thunderstorm, which deeply saddened him. Over time, he became a supporter of Nell's Village Improvement Society and maintained his unique, blunt, yet friendly relationship with his neighbors.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school
unit: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school, securing the position largely due to the influence of his uncle, who was a school trustee. During his tenure, he focused much of his attention on preparing older students for the Regent's Academy entrance exam and courting Sukey Pullen. His favoritism toward Sukey and poor classroom discipline drew criticism from locals, and he frequently punished students unjustly or through public humiliation. During a notable classroom incident, he mocked Nell Harcourt, prompting her to smash her slate over Hugh Carrow's head; although Hugh took the blame, Pidgeon forced Nell to stand on a dais beneath a harsh inscription on the blackboard. On another occasion, he made Nell sit next to Hugh Carrow as a punishment for being late. Aside from his teaching, Pidgeon participated in local events, delivering a speech at a Brierley Debating Club concert and reciting Mark Antony's address over Caesar's body. At the end of the school year, he delivered a moving farewell speech to the students before resigning his position, which was subsequently taken over by a female teacher, Miss Agnes Thorne.

label: History
value: Ezra Hale was studying theology at St. Columbia.
unit: While studying theology at St. Columbia, Ezra Hale spent a summer serving as a student minister for the Point Prospect Mission Church. During his stay at Prospect Point, he met Cressida Lindsay, with whom he quickly formed a close and affectionate friendship. Although Cressida initially resisted his plain looks and lack of wealth, Ezra's sincerity and powerful preaching deeply impressed her. Following his graduation from St. Columbia, Ezra accepted a post managing a mission church in the Tanner Street slums. After a period of courtship, he proposed to Cressida, and the two were eventually married in June beneath a honeysuckle trellis at Echo Cottage.

During his stay at Prospect Point, he met Cressida Lindsay, with whom he quickly formed a close and affectionate friendship. Although Cressida initially resisted his plain looks and lack of wealth, Ezra's sincerity and powerful preaching deeply impressed her. Following his graduation from St. Columbia, Ezra accepted a post managing a mission church in the Tanner Street slums. After a period of courtship, he proposed to Cressida, and the two were eventually married in June beneath a honeysuckle trellis at Echo Cottage.

label: History
value: Robin grew up in Nova Scotia
unit: Robin grew up in Nova Scotia as part of a large family with several sets of twins. After his mother passed away, he and his twin sister Lucy were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters in Brierley. He quickly proved to be a handful, regularly indulging in pranks such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, pushing his sister into a pigpen, and placing a toad in Thirza's bed. Despite his mischief, he developed a deep affection for Nell Harcourt and Thirza. When he began attending Brierley school, he proved to be a lively student who formed strong friendships, particularly with Milty Gammon. He also enjoyed visiting his neighbor, Mr. Pettifer, and developed a fondness for farm chores, eventually aspiring to manage the farm himself. Upon learning of his uncle's death in British Columbia, he remained permanently in the care of Thirza at Grey Shutters.

label: History
value: Rosalind Penrose lived in seclusion at Echo Cottage in Middle Welby.
unit: Rosalind Penrose lived for decades in seclusion at Echo Cottage in Middle Welby following a broken engagement with Stephen Stanhope in her youth. To cope with her isolation, she frequently engaged in imaginative games and hosted pretend tea parties for non-existent guests. Eventually, Nell Harcourt accidentally stumbled upon Echo Cottage and struck up a close friendship with her. After learning of Rosalind's past, Nell helped arrange a reunion between Rosalind and Stephen Stanhope when he returned to St. Brendan's Island to visit his son Cedric. The two reconciled, fell in love anew, and were married twenty-five years after their initial breakup in an outdoor ceremony at Echo Cottage. Following the wedding, she and Stephen departed for a journey to the Pacific Coast, planning to reside in Boston while keeping Echo Cottage for summer visits.

unit: Rosalind Penrose lived for decades in seclusion at Echo Cottage in Middle Welby following a broken engagement with Stephen Stanhope in her youth. To cope with her isolation, she frequently engaged in imaginative games and hosted pretend tea parties for non-existent guests. Eventually, Nell Harcourt accidentally stumbled upon Echo Cottage and struck up a close friendship with her. After learning of Rosalind's past, Nell helped arrange a reunion between Rosalind and Stephen Stanhope when he returned to St. Brendan's Island to visit his son Cedric. The two reconciled, fell in love anew, and were married twenty-five years after their initial breakup in an outdoor ceremony at Echo Cottage. Following the wedding, she and Stephen departed for a journey to the Pacific Coast, planning to reside in Boston while keeping Echo Cottage for summer visits.

label: History
value: Rufus Vane operated a small sawmill.
unit: Rufus Vane operated a small sawmill up river and resided in a desolate clearing surrounded by stumps. He married Lorna Ainslie after coercing her into the union by threatening to foreclose on her widowed mother's farm mortgage. During their marriage, his household took in the orphan Nell Harcourt for over two years to help care for their eight young children, including three sets of twins. After Rufus passed away, his household was dissolved and his children were distributed among family members, leading Nell to be sent to the Marden asylum. It was later revealed that Rufus had sailed to Cuba on the Four Sisters, contracted yellow fever, and died there thirteen years prior to the events at Seven Gulls; the man who had returned to Seven Gulls in his place and lived under his name as an invalid for eleven years was actually his cousin, Laurence Vane.

label: History
value: Tabitha served as the general servant.
unit: Tabitha initially served as the general servant for old Miss Lavinia Pembroke at Port Marlow. Following Miss Pembroke's death, she eventually entered the service of Hugh and Nell Carrow at Hollowmere in Seven Gulls Harbor. She quickly established herself as the unyielding ruler of the kitchen, taking complete charge of the household cooking and baking. When Nell fell dangerously ill after giving birth to her youngest child, Harcourt, Tabitha nursed the fragile infant with maternal devotion, claiming a special bond with him over his own mother. She continued to manage the household with an iron hand, managing the Carrow children, scolding their flaws, and fiercely protecting them from others.

She later welcomed two young orphans, the Farrow twins Robin and Lucy, taking on their care and upbringing. Eventually, she saw Nell graduate from college and marry Hugh Carrow, the son of her former youthful sweetheart.

label: History
value: Agnes Thorne is hired as a teacher at Brierley School.
unit: Agnes Thorne is hired as the first female teacher at Brierley School, taking over the classroom in autumn. She quickly earns the affection and devotion of her pupils, including Nell Harcourt, through her gentle and encouraging methods. She introduces novel educational activities such as field days for studying nature, physical culture exercises, and bi-weekly recitation afternoons. After catching Nell reading a novel during class, she gently reprimands her for dishonesty and time-misuse, securing Nell's promise to refrain from reading inappropriate books. During the autumn, she organizes a student Christmas concert in the hall to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag, which proves to be a grand success. She also forms an extra study class after school hours for her advanced pupils—Nell, Hugh Carrow, Opal Pettigrew, Odette Pullen, Flossie Tulk, Wilfred Mott, and Elias Purdy MacKinnon—to prepare them for the Regent's Entrance Examination. Though offered a position at her home district's grade school at the end of the year, she chooses to remain at Brierley to see her entrance class through their final year. She continues to guide her students through their rigorous studies, and at the conclusion of the second year, her entrance class achieves complete success, with Nell winning the Avery Scholarship and Hugh capturing the medal.

She is highly practical, industrious, and takes great pride in her skill as a needlewoman.

value: Winifred lived for decades as an unmarried woman.
unit: Winifred lived for decades as an unmarried woman in her green-painted house on the Seven Gulls road, known throughout the area for her blunt speech, her expert sewing skills, and her willingness to care for sick neighbors. She regularly attended Presbyterian services and frequently voiced her distaste for Methodists and men. She developed a close friendship with Nell Harcourt, whom she supported during her years as a teacher and throughout her marriage to Dr. Hugh Carrow. When Lorna Vane was left in hardship, Winifred actively advocated for her and helped arrange for a paying boarder to stay at her cottage. In her late fifties, after years of rejecting suitors and insisting she would never marry, she surprised her friends by accepting the proposal of her long-time admirer, Ambrose Kerr, and getting married.
